summary: The end-to-end AddVoter witness completed (CheckRun 75d8b1b6b9f544acac8a3a21d02ff4e9, exit 0) and confirmed the source-decided account on a real cluster, including the availability consequence. The public join succeeded and both views agree the added member holds a vote: the leader's latest configuration and the new node's own configuration each report suffrage Voter, with three voters in the configuration. With one original voter disconnected, a command applied afterwards still committed, and the commitment arithmetic makes that decisive: with three voters and one of the original two unreachable, the majority of two can only be satisfied if the freshly added member acknowledged the new entry, so its match index was counted. That is precisely the protection the AddVoter documentation promises and the implementation does not provide - the doc comment says the server joins as a staging member promoted once it is ready, while the member counts in elections and in the leader's quorum from the entry that adds it, and the command table plus the unit expectations show the immediate-voter behaviour is what the library intends and tests. I recorded the observation as a fact, wrote an interpretation that now rests on an execution rather than reading alone, and kept the scope narrow: no consensus-safety rule is broken because log comparison still prevents a less up-to-date member from winning, so the cost is availability arithmetic and caller expectations. I also queued the control that keeps the harness identical but joins the node with AddNonvoter, where the same disconnect should leave no reachable majority and the command should fail to commit; that control is what keeps the quorum inference honest, since if it also committed the discriminator would be wrong and the account would need rework. The three earlier witnessed findings, the configuration index, duties lost at shutdown, and the vote-less transfer with its control and reproduction, remain recorded and unaffected.
